title: NeoRadar controlled airspace limits
description: data/cas.json in a vAcc's sector source, beside topsky/ and euroscope_data/: the class and the vertical limits of the controlled airspace the sector file draws, which the sector file itself never carries. The shapes come from the sector file: each entry names an [ARTCC HIGH] or [ARTCC LOW] group of the .sct, `neoradar-cli convert` joins that group's line segments into the faces they enclose, gives each face the limits of the volume that holds it, and writes datasets/cas.geojson (`@schemas/datasets/cas.schema.json`) into the package, where the airspace infringement net reads it. Optional: no file means no CAS dataset, and the net keeps its zones or the online sectors. Written by hand from the AIP, each entry naming its source; the vAcc's copy is the master. Checked by `convert` and refused before anything is written: a name the sector file does not draw, a volume point that lies in none of its group's faces, two volumes in one face, and more than one volume with no point. A face no volume claims is left out and named in neoradar-cli.log.

value.description: Feet for FT, hundreds of feet for FL; absent for SFC and UNL.

uom.description: FT: an altitude above mean sea level, judged on the QNH altitude. FL: a flight level, judged on the pressure altitude. SFC: the surface, as a lower limit. UNL: unlimited, as an upper limit.

part.description: The part as the AIP names it (LONDON TMA 1). Absent, the volume takes the entry's name. It is what the alert text prints.

at.description: [latitude, longitude] in decimal degrees, WGS84: a point inside the face of the group this volume is. Needed when the group draws more than one face; an entry whose one volume has no point gives its limits to every face of the group.

name.description: The group's name exactly as the .sct writes it in [ARTCC HIGH] or [ARTCC LOW] (EGLL London Heathrow CTR).

source.description: Where the classes and limits were copied from, with its edition (UK AIP AD 2.EGLL AD 2.17, AIRAC 2026-10-29).
